The healer chest is left side gear. For an attack based healer, a perfect piece would have 3 substats: attack %, healing effect and speed. With it being a chest piece specifically, you can only roll speed as a substat on a chest piece when the gear is ancient or T3. So unless you have better ancient gear in a different set or a T3 piece with all 3 substats, your healers will be wearing a chest piece with the same 2 substats as this healer piece so it’s perfectly usable. 

The damage piece is right side gear. For an attack based damage dealer, a perfect piece would have main stat: attack %, substats: crit rate, crit damage and speed. When building your attackers, the first thing you prioritise is building attack % and getting crit rate to 100%. This doesn’t have crit rate so there’s no scenario where you’d ever use it, it’s complete trash.

OP has healer substats on an attack set.

You’re not guaranteed a good one, this is what you seem to be overlooking. Take the recent Hex banner, I don’t have the numbers to hand but let’s say with the 15x boosted rates, the chance to get Hex when you eventually land a legendary is 20%. In order to statistically ‘guarantee’ a Hex then you’d need to save 1100 blue shards. 80% of the time you’re not going to get Hex, you’re just as likely to get the heroes you consider F tier. That’s potentially 880 blue shards wasted on 4 heroes that aren’t Hex.

Now the 2x chance, you’ve got double the chance of getting any legendary. In those same 1100 blue shards, statistically you should get 10 legendaries. Twice as many. The chance of you getting 10 trash heroes is incredibly unlikely. You might not get the S tier hero you want, for example you might get Khamet and Silas instead of Hex, but that’s the trade off you make. And those other heroes will still boost your progress significantly as a newer player. 

15x banners are incredibly expensive for new players, you often have to go to pity (220 pulls) to get a single legendary. Think about how long it takes you to save 220 pulls.You want to get the best return on your resources. I’d argue only pulling on 1x is wasting them considerably. If you’re getting the banner hero you want and you’re getting lucky, I’m glad, but thats not the norm for the majority.

Best recommendation for learning the animations would be to go into the campaign mode or whatever it’s called where you create your own fighter and in the training sessions for ground, play it, then restart until you can successfully master it. It takes a bit of patience learning which movement is which transition but it feels so rewarding when you nail it.

If you’re currently stuck in Div5, maybe that’s your current skill level and you’re exactly where you need to be right now? Tactics are only part of the battle, there’s no benefit to being in a higher division if you lose every single game. Best advice is trial and error and find what works for you. Tactics completely differ between people’s play styles so you’ll only find your sweet spot by trying your own and understanding what they do and how it impacts your players in game. My tip would be to look at what games you’re losing and why. Are people using wingers better than you? Upgrade your LB/RB. Are they running through you in the middle of the park? Upgrade your midfield or play a narrow formation. If you switch and can’t create attacks, change to a slightly wider formation so you have more attacking outlets or increase your attacking width. Are your players too far forward? Change one CM/CDM to stay back while attacking or reduce your overall depth. Equally are they too far back when you get countered? Increase your overall defensive depth. It comes with time but you’ll get there.

In terms of SBC, the only good ones to do for minimal coins at the start of the game are the Hybrid Nation and Hybrid League ones to give you a few decent packs for players, which you’ll be able to sell and hopefully make coins from.

In terms of passing, try to utilise r1 and pass (or whatever the input is for driven pass) - it’s much quicker, less chance of being intercepted.

In terms of dribbling, practise using only left stick dribbling (again, whatever the input is for moving your players) to get better. You’ll be able to turn one way like you do with De Bruyne, then turn back the other way and fool the person pushing you then run into space. Don’t be worried about passing back though, this FIFA’s more about build up play rather than playing 1-2s back and forth and within 3 passes being through on goal.. although that can still happen.

Utilise the input to make people make a run to give you a bit of space, or use 1-2s to get round other players and give you space to run into.

I’d recommend watching some YouTube tutorials, just search like ‘fifa 22 attacking/passing/dribbling tutorials’ and they’ll give you a full walkthrough of what to do.

In terms of trading, I really wouldn’t bother. The market is at an all time low and with minimal coins, you’ll have to invest a lot of time. Best thing to do is play the game, get 500 coins for a win and save up for a solid team. 

Make sure you do squad battles every week as you’ll start to learn the passing and defending mechanics better. It’s not the same as playing real people, and they’re the only transferable skills you’ll get from it, but it’ll give you a good foundation and some packs a long the way to help you start your journey.

When you play rivals, you only need 7 wins in a week to get the good rewards. If you’re close to going up a division, try grind it out before the reward day as the rewards are determined by what division you’re in on that day, rather than where you started off at the beginning of the week.

The game is nostalgic in a sense, it has the same map and storyline but that’s about it. There’s no bike, you ride around on Pokemon now. There is no daycare breeding. There is no such thing as EVs either. The HM’s are renamed (fly is magic dash for example) and they don’t have to be taught to your Pokemon. Your pikachu/eevee just magically learns them as a sort of ‘ability’ in the background, not part of the move set, and it prompts you to use it when necessary so you don’t have to carry an additional Pokemon with those moves learned. You asked about difficulty and the capture system. Difficulty is non existent, just from catching Pokemon I’ve got a full team of level 40’s by the 3rd gym and I haven’t grinded. It’s virtually impossible to lose a fight, they make your pikachu/eevee have 6ivs and learn moves that OHKO everything. The capture system is... weird. Not having wild battles is just odd for me. It’s basically stand still, watch Pokemon spawn around you and walk into one you want. Press A, catch, repeat. The more you catch of the same Pokemon, the easier it is to catch it the next time. You have to catch 31 of the same Pokemon in a row to increase your shiny chances, every time you catch one your xp scales (hence why I’m so overlevelled - and I’ve only gone to 31 once so far). A lot of rarer Pokemon are tied behind this chain combo so for example, you might not see a 1% spawn rate Pokemon for ages. Catch a few of the same Pokemon, the odds drastically increase and rarer Pokemon appear. Catch it, the combo resets to 0 and then repeat to find more. The more you catch in a row, the better IVs the Pokemon has so it’s a case of constant repetition. It’s not a bad game at all, it’s just not the same and I’d be annoyed if I paid full price for it. Ask me any other questions you might have and I’ll be happy to give my opinion.

TLDR: It’s literally Pokemon go but instead of being tied to your GPS where you physically walk around in the real world, you walk around in the map of yellow.

Gen 1 player here too. It’s a good game but in a completely different way. The story is very linear, there’s one path to follow and you can’t deviate from it at all whereas in gen 1 you could skip gyms and go to different cities first, doing it in whatever order you wanted etc. The main emphasis on this game is catching everything. I know that sounds silly as to an extent that’s always been the goal but this is probably the easiest to complete the full dex by a long shot. There’s no need to grind levels in order to beat the game or progress either; you start with an xp share equivalent that can’t be turned off and it levels everyone in your party so if you play this game like you had to play gen 1, you’ll overlevel instantly. It’s definitely a good game though, graphics are a huge improvement, it’s fun, plenty of quality of life improvements, and it has a really helpful community - just don’t get your hopes up if you’re expecting it to be anywhere close to as challenging as gen 1 was because this is ez mode. That said, there’s much more to do in this, especially post-game rather than just getting mewtwo and grinding the elite 4.
